name: Read a paper road map
blurb: Folding, legend, scale, grid references and the ability to plan a route before you set off. It also builds the mental model of a region that satnav actively prevents.
gear: A paper road atlas or a folded regional map
steps: Learn the legend properly: road classifications, distances between junctions, gradients, and what the symbols mean.
Learn the scale and how to convert map distance to real distance quickly with your thumb or a scrap of paper.
Learn the grid and index system so you can find a named place in seconds.
Plan a real route: write down the road numbers and junction names in sequence, as a strip map.
Navigate a real journey with the map only, no phone.
Learn to refold it properly, which is genuinely a skill.
tips: Turn the map to match your direction of travel. Reading a map upside down is where most errors happen.
Note the road numbers and the next big town, not the individual turns. That is how signs are actually labelled.
proof: You drive an unfamiliar 100 km route using only a paper map, without a wrong turn.
